A Dream Start and VAR Drama The match ignited within the opening sixty seconds. Arsenal wasted no time establishing dominance as Riccardo Calafiori found the back of the net with a clinical left-footed finish, following a sharp assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly . The goal was briefly held in the balance during a tense VAR review, but the referee eventually pointed to the center spot, confirming the lead. Manchester City struggled to find their rhythm early on, evidenced by Phil Foden receiving a yellow card for unsportsmanlike conduct as frustrations began to simmer. As the first half progressed, the visitors' tactical discipline kept the hosts at bay. The City midfield, usually so dominant in possession, found itself crowded out by a hungry Arsenal press that refused to let the game settle into a predictable pattern. Clinical Execution and Goal-Line Clearances The Gunners doubled their advantage in the 28th minute through a beautifully orchestrated team move. Martin Ødegaard provided the vision with a key pass to Christos Tzolis , who delivered a perfect cross for Kai Havertz to head home. The drama intensified ten minutes later when Riccardo Calafiori was booked for diving in the penalty box—a controversial decision that denied Arsenal a chance for a third from the spot. Late in the first half, both ends of the pitch saw incredible defensive heroics. Martin Ødegaard saw a certain goal hacked off the line, only for Jeremy Doku to experience the same frustration at the other end moments later. These narrow escapes kept the scoreline at 2-0 heading into the interval, leaving the door slightly ajar for a potential comeback. Ødegaard Seals the Deal Any hopes of a Manchester City recovery were effectively extinguished just three minutes after the restart. Martin Ødegaard , who had been the architect of so much of his team's success, turned scorer by finishing with his left foot after excellent work from Tzolis and Lewis-Skelly . The 3-0 deficit prompted Pep Guardiola to make sweeping changes, including replacing Erling Haaland with Omar Marmoush , but the momentum remained firmly with the North Londoners. Despite late pressure from Antoine Semenyo and creative sparks from Rayan Cherki , the Arsenal defense remained resolute. Gabriel and Piero Hincapie made crucial interventions to protect the clean sheet. In front of a crowd of 58,056 , the final whistle confirmed a comprehensive and deserved victory for the Gunners, as they marched into the next round with a performance of genuine authority.

The Devon Derby returned to the Carabao Cup stage on August 10, 2026 , as Plymouth Argyle hosted Exeter City in a high-stakes encounter. Both teams sought to assert local dominance in a match that remained balanced and unpredictable until the very final moments of play. A Tense Exchange of Chances From the opening whistle, Plymouth Argyle looked to dictate the tempo, with Harvey White testing the waters early with a long-range effort. The home side continued to pile on the pressure as Ronan Curtis and Aribim Pepple forced Exeter City goalkeeper Jack Bycroft into several crucial saves. Despite the territorial advantage for the Pilgrims, Exeter remained dangerous on the break, with Charlie Cummins nearly finding the target from a set-piece situation that flew just over the bar. As the first half progressed, the physical nature of the derby became evident. Charlie Cummins received an early booking for a heavy challenge, signaling the intensity of the midfield battle. While Mathias Ross and Pepple continued to search for the breakthrough before the interval, the visitors’ defense held firm, ensuring the scoreline remained level at the break after a series of blocked attempts and narrow misses. Momentum Shifts and a Costly Red Card The second half saw Exeter City grow in confidence, creating a flurry of opportunities. Taylor Perry and Andrew Oluwabori both came close to silencing the home crowd, with the latter seeing a headed effort rise just too high. Plymouth's manager responded by introducing fresh legs, bringing on Matthew Sorinola and Julio Pleguezuelo to regain control of the flanks and revitalize an attack that was struggling to find a clinical edge. The game reached a turning point in the 87th minute when Ethan Sutherland , who had been cautioned only nine minutes earlier, committed a tactical foul that resulted in a second yellow card. His dismissal left Exeter City a man down for the closing stages, forcing them into a defensive shell as Plymouth Argyle launched a final, desperate assault on the Grecians' goal. Stoppage Time Fireworks Just as the match seemed destined for a penalty shootout, the deadlock was finally broken in the 92nd minute. A pinpoint corner from Harvey White found the head of Alex Hartridge , who powered his effort into the top left corner from close range. The breakthrough sent the home supporters into a frenzy, but the drama was far from over as the clock ticked deep into added time. With Exeter pushing everyone forward in search of an equalizer, Plymouth Argyle struck again in the 94th minute. Freddie Issaka spearheaded a lightning-fast counter-attack, squaring the ball to Aribim Pepple in the center of the box. Pepple made no mistake, slotting the ball home to secure a 2-0 victory. Although Josh Gordon forced one final save from Murphy Cooper in the dying seconds, the result was already sealed, sending Plymouth through to the next round.
